title: bug: acquire_resource and wait_for_resource lease a resource to a BACKLOG, AWAITING_APPROVAL, DONE or ARCHIVED task, a status report_blocked refuses and grantNextLeases and the reaper skip, so live waiters queue behind a lease no other grant path would issue until the 5-minute reaper sweep
description:
Filed by defect hunt #9 (task-66961b32), lane: daemon resource tool family. All paths are under packages/moe-daemon/ unless noted.

PROBLEM
- Three grant-side siblings apply one eligibility rule: the task must be PLANNING, WORKING, REVIEW or BLOCKED (RESOURCE_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES and isResourceTaskEligible, src/state/resourceStore.ts:57-67).
  - report_blocked refuses a non-blockable status BEFORE its resource arm (src/tools/reportBlocked.ts:104-113: "a queued lease on such a row would hand a grant to a status the grant path cannot restore").
  - grantNextLeases filters the queue (resourceStore.ts:468-470: "Every grant path must recheck eligibility, not just the periodic reaper.").
  - reapResources revokes an ineligible task's lease and queue entry (resourceStore.ts:626 and :635), but only from runBlockedTimeoutSweep (src/state/sweeps.ts:559), which runs every 300000 ms (sweeps.ts:58).
- The direct grant skips the rule. acquire_resource (src/tools/acquireResource.ts:42-44) and wait_for_resource (src/tools/waitForResource.ts:65-67) check only that the task exists, plus assertWorkerOwns, which is a no-op on an unassigned row (src/util/enforcement.ts:44). Every human-gated row is unassigned. state.acquireResource then grants on capacity and dependencies alone (resourceStore.ts:245), and it renews an existing lease on such a row (resourceStore.ts:229-243).
- Result: a lease is held by a row the daemon itself treats as orphaned. A live WORKING task that acquires next gets granted:false, position 1, nextTool moe.report_blocked, and parks until the next sweep.
- Audience: TOOL_AUDIENCE [W, Q] (src/tools/index.ts:256 and :259).
- Trigger: a session that is still running after a human or governor moved its row to BACKLOG or DONE, acquiring a capacity-1 resource such as git-land-moe-work-2026-10-24 or jetbrains-gradle.

EVIDENCE (HEAD 39bec237, run in a git-archive snapshot outside the shared checkout)
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-66961b32/A/zzHuntA_acquireIneligible.test.ts, with its output beside it (.out.txt). The architect re-ran it in /tmp/hunt-6696-snap; see /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-66961b32/verify-architect.txt.
- `npx vitest run src/tools/zzHuntA_acquireIneligible.test.ts` gives Tests 5 failed | 1 passed (6):
  - acquire_resource on a DONE task: expected { granted: undefined, holders: [] }, received granted: true, holders ["task-done:DONE"]. BACKLOG and AWAITING_APPROVAL fail the same way.
  - wait_for_resource on a DONE task: granted true, holders ["task-done:DONE"].
  - a WORKING task acquiring afterwards: received { granted: false, position: 1, nextTool: "moe.report_blocked" }.
  - The passing control: reapResources() drops the DONE lease (reaped 1).

FIX DIRECTION
- Refuse at the tool level, mirroring reportBlocked.ts:104-113.
  - Export the eligibility predicate (or the status set) from resourceStore.ts.
  - In both tools, after the notFound check and before assertWorkerOwns, throw invalidState(`Task <id>`, status, 'PLANNING/WORKING/REVIEW/BLOCKED to lease a resource ...').
  - Write nothing on that path: no lease, no queue entry, no waiter and no touchWorker.
- Do not move the check into resourceStore.acquireResource, because resourceStore.test.ts:229-245 seeds DONE and ARCHIVED leases through the store to test the reaper.
- REVIEW stays eligible, so the wrapper's git-land acquire after complete_task is unaffected.

FILES
- src/tools/acquireResource.ts
- src/tools/waitForResource.ts
- src/state/resourceStore.ts (export only)
- new src/tools/acquireResource.ineligible.test.ts

Out of scope: docs/MCP_SERVER.md.
definitionOfDone: `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/acquireResource.ineligible.test.ts` passes in a snapshot outside the shared checkout. It asserts that acquire_resource on a BACKLOG, an AWAITING_APPROVAL, a DONE and an ARCHIVED task each rejects with codeName INVALID_STATE and a message naming the status, and that state.getResource(<id>) then has no holder and no queue entry for that task.

The same file asserts that wait_for_resource on a DONE task rejects the same way and leaves no activeResourceWaiters entry for the caller, and that a WORKING task's acquire_resource on the same resource afterwards returns granted: true.
`npx vitest run src/tools/acquireResource.test.ts src/tools/waitForResource.test.ts src/state/resourceStore.test.ts src/tools/reportBlocked.test.ts` stays green in the same snapshot.

implementationPlan.description: Tests first: create packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/acquireResource.ineligible.test.ts (vitest + ToolTestHarness, modelled on waitForResource.test.ts). Fixture (beforeEach): setupMoeFolder, createEpic; task-live WORKING assigned worker-1; unassigned ineligible rows task-backlog BACKLOG, task-awaiting AWAITING_APPROVAL, task-done DONE, task-archived ARCHIVED; unassigned eligible controls task-planning PLANNING, task-review REVIEW (as complete_task leaves it), task-blocked BLOCKED with blockedFromStatus WORKING; workers worker-1 (CODING, currentTaskId task-live) and worker-x (IDLE, the stale session); await state.load(); mock postToGeneral/postToRoleChannel/postSystemMessage. afterEach: resolve+delete every activeResourceWaiters entry (copy waitForResource.test.ts), vi.restoreAllMocks, h.cleanup. Shared matcher refusal(status) = { codeName: 'INVALID_STATE', message: expect.stringContaining(`is in ${status} state, expected PLANNING/WORKING/REVIEW/BLOCKED`) }. Prefix every title with its id. (i1) it.each over the 4 ineligible rows: with vi.spyOn(h.state, 'touchWorker'), acquire_resource {resourceId:'box', taskId, workerId:'worker-x'} rejects toMatchObject(refusal(status)); h.state.getResource('box') is null (not even a resource record was written); touchWorker not called; then acquire_resource for task-live/worker-1 returns granted:true (DoD 1). (i2) task-live takes box first; the DONE row's acquire is refused; box.holders map to ['task-live'] and box.queue equals [] (the busy path never queues it). (w1) wait_for_resource {task-done, worker-x, timeoutMs:1000} rejects with refusal('DONE'); getResource('box') null; activeResourceWaiters.has('worker-x') false; touchWorker not called; then task-live's acquire_resource returns granted:true (DoD 2). (w2) lock recheck: FIRST take the lock, const holding = h.state.runExclusive(async () => { await gate; await h.state.updateTask('task-live', { status: 'BACKLOG' }); }), THEN call wait_for_resource for task-live/worker-1 and attach .catch((error: unknown) => error) at once (no unhandled rejection), open the gate, await holding; the caught outcome matches refusal('BACKLOG'), getResource('box') is null, no waiter for worker-1. It works because the handler's pre-check runs synchronously before its first await (row still WORKING) and its locked section runs after the status change. (e1) it.each over [task-planning, worker-x], [task-live, worker-1], [task-review, worker-x], [task-blocked, worker-x]: acquire_resource returns granted:true and holders are exactly [taskId]. REVIEW must stay leasable: the worktree wrapper takes git-land-<target> after complete_task. About 120 lines; no other test file changes. Reference copy, dry-run green on the fixed sources and RED on HEAD a028ec65 (Tests 7 failed | 4 passed (11), only the (e1) rows pass): /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-9f34bac5/reference-acquireResource.ineligible.test.ts. Write your own bytes with Edit/Write (global rail: TOOL witness).

Export the rule and refuse in acquire_resource. packages/moe-daemon/src/state/resourceStore.ts: change ONLY the declaration to `export const RESOURCE_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES: ReadonlySet<TaskStatus> = new Set<TaskStatus>([...])` (same four statuses in the same order: PLANNING, WORKING, REVIEW, BLOCKED) and say in its doc comment that the grant path, the reaper and the acquire/wait tools share it. isResourceTaskEligible, grantNextLeases, reapResources and the store's acquireResource stay byte-identical: NO check in the store, because resourceStore.test.ts:229-245 seeds DONE/ARCHIVED leases through it to test the reaper, and report_blocked already refuses those statuses before its resource arm. packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/acquireResource.ts: add an exported `assertResourceTaskEligible(task: Task): void` that returns when RESOURCE_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES.has(task.status) and otherwise throws invalidState(`Task ${task.id}`, task.status, `${[...RESOURCE_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES].join('/')} to lease a resource. No grant path serves a lease on this row and the lease reaper revokes one: take the lease for the task your seat is working on, or move this row back with moe.set_task_status first. Nothing was written`) (import type Task from '../types/schema.js'; invalidState from '../util/errors.js'), with a short doc comment naming the shared rule. Call it in the handler right after the notFound check, BEFORE assertWorkerOwns and touchWorker. Error handling: the refusal is a coded MoeError (INVALID_STATE, data {entity, currentState, expectedState}) thrown before any write, so there is no resource record, lease, queue entry, RESOURCE_* activity or heartbeat; the input schema and the granted/queued response shapes stay unchanged. Leave the tool description and docs/MCP_SERVER.md alone (out of scope).

Refuse in wait_for_resource, twice. packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/waitForResource.ts: import { assertResourceTaskEligible } from './acquireResource.js' (no import cycle: acquireResource.ts imports nothing from waitForResource.ts). (a) Call it right after the notFound check, BEFORE assertWorkerOwns, touchWorker, the shouldContinue check and the cancel-and-replace of an existing waiter, so a refused call writes nothing and leaves any earlier waiter of the seat untouched. (b) Inside the state.runExclusive callback, after the existing shouldContinue check and before state.acquireResource, re-read the row: `const current = state.getTask(taskId); if (!current) throw notFound('Task', taskId); assertResourceTaskEligible(current);` with a one-line comment that the first check ran outside the lock. Why (b): wait_for_resource is blocking:true, so McpAdapter dispatches it WITHOUT the state mutex (mem:gotcha-daemon-global-mutex-dispatch); a row moved to BACKLOG/DONE, or deleted, while the call waited for the lock would otherwise still be granted. acquire_resource needs no second check because it is dispatched under the mutex. Error handling: a throw inside runExclusive releases the lock in its finally and rejects the handler with the same INVALID_STATE (NOT_FOUND for a deleted row); neither refusal path registers a waiter, and the granted/timed-out/cancelled response shapes are unchanged. Reference diff for steps 2-3 (35 changed lines): /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-9f34bac5/reference-fix.diff.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.acquire_resource and moe.wait_for_resource refuse, with INVALID_STATE naming the row's status, any task that is not PLANNING, WORKING, REVIEW or BLOCKED (the RESOURCE_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES rule grantNextLeases and reapResources already apply), before writing anything: no resource record, lease, queue entry, activity row, heartbeat or waiter. wait_for_resource re-checks the row inside its locked section, so a row that leaves an eligible status (or is deleted) while the call waits for the state lock gets no lease. Eligible rows are leased and queued exactly as before.
acceptanceCriteria: acquire_resource on a BACKLOG, AWAITING_APPROVAL, DONE or ARCHIVED task rejects with codeName INVALID_STATE and a message containing 'is in <STATUS> state, expected PLANNING/WORKING/REVIEW/BLOCKED'; state.getResource('box') stays null, touchWorker is not called, and a WORKING task's acquire_resource afterwards is granted.
Behind a busy holder a refused row takes no queue entry: holders stay ['task-live'] and the queue stays [].

wait_for_resource on a DONE task rejects the same way, writes nothing, leaves no activeResourceWaiters entry for the caller and calls no touchWorker; a WORKING task's acquire_resource on the same resource afterwards returns granted: true.
A row moved to BACKLOG while wait_for_resource waits for the state lock is refused with INVALID_STATE and gets no lease and no waiter.
PLANNING, WORKING, REVIEW (unassigned) and BLOCKED rows are still granted through acquire_resource.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Check inside resourceStore.acquireResource: rejected, because resourceStore.test.ts:229-245 seeds DONE/ARCHIVED leases through the store to test the reaper, and report_blocked's resource arm is already status-gated. (2) A copied status list in each tool: rejected; export the store's RESOURCE_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES (ReadonlySet) so the grant path, the reaper and the tools share one rule. (3) One exported helper assertResourceTaskEligible in acquireResource.ts, reused by waitForResource.ts at both call sites: one message and three call sites, and resourceStore.ts stays an export-only change as the row asks. (4) Pre-check only in wait_for_resource: insufficient, because the tool is blocking and runs outside the state mutex, so a status change while it waits for the lock would still be granted. Hence the in-lock recheck. (5) Tool description or docs/MCP_SERVER.md edits: out of scope per the row; the refusal message is self-explanatory.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: McpAdapter runs non-blocking tools inside the global reentrant state mutex, so acquire_resource's single check is atomic with its write; wait_for_resource (blocking: true) takes the lock only around state.acquireResource. assertWorkerOwns is a no-op on unassigned rows, which is why human-gated rows slipped through. touchWorker writes the worker file, so 'no heartbeat' is observable with vi.spyOn(h.state, 'touchWorker'). An async handler runs synchronously up to its first await, so a test can hold the lock (h.state.runExclusive plus a gate), call the handler (its pre-check passes on the old status), change the status inside the held section, then release, which deterministically exercises the in-lock recheck. Architect dry-run artifacts (reference diff, test, gate, RED/GREEN/mutant results): /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-9f34bac5/.
